extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and citizens interested in constitutional design and republican government
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts normative principles for structuring republican government to preserve liberty — e.g., separation of powers, checks and balances, federalism, and protections for minorities. The page is Federalist No. 51 (James Madison) presenting design criteria for constitutional systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior structure must supply for inadequate external provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The defect of exterior provisions being inadequate must be supplied by contriving the interior structure of the Government so that its several constituent parts, by their mutual relations, are the means of keeping each other in their proper places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General prescription: design internal institutional relations so branches check each other; the essay offers this as the central design criterion when external (popular) controls are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each department should have 'a will of its own'
rubrics_metrics.description: Each department should be constituted so that the members of each have as little agency as possible in the appointment of the members of the others; each should have a separate will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal: appointments for Executive, Legislative, Judiciary drawn from the People through channels having no communication. Practical deviations may be necessary, especially for the Judiciary (see judicial exception). The text notes difficulties and expenses of strict separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize dependence of departments on others for emoluments
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each department should be as little dependent as possible on those of the others for the emoluments annexed to their offices; financial dependence undermines independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example/guidance: If Executive or Judges are dependent on the Legislature for pay, their independence in other respects would be 'merely nominal' — thus compensation arrangements must protect independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give officers constitutional means and personal motives to resist encroachments ('ambition must be made to counteract ambition')
rubrics_metrics.description: The best security against concentration of power is to give those who administer each department the necessary constitutional means and personal motives to resist encroachments of the others; ambition should counteract ambition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design devices: structure offices so private interest aligns with constitutional rights of the office; rely on competing ambitions and interests as internal checks rather than solely on virtue or good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on the people is primary control, but auxiliary precautions are necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependence on the People is the primary control on the Government; experience shows auxiliary precautions are also necessary to prevent abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: do not rely solely on popular control; supplement with institutional checks, separation, and structural safeguards to constrain government and oblige it to control itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide the Legislature into different branches with distinct modes of election
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Legislative authority necessarily predominates in a republic, the remedy is to divide the Legislature into different branches and render them, by different modes of election and different principles of action, as little connected with each other as their common functions admit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: bicameral or multi-branch legislatures reduce concentration of legislative power; election methods and principles of action should differ to create independent incentives and checks between branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortify the Executive via qualified connections rather than an absolute negative
rubrics_metrics.description: An absolute negative (veto) on the Legislature by the Executive may be neither safe nor sufficient; a qualified connection between the Executive and the weaker branch of the Legislature may supply necessary support for Executive rights without detaching that branch from its own principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: favor institutional devices that connect the Executive to a legislative counterweight (e.g., a weaker legislative branch) in limited, qualified ways rather than granting an unchecked absolute veto that can be abused or weakly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial appointment exceptions: prioritize qualifications and permanent tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: In constituting the Judiciary, it may be inexpedient to insist rigidly on appointment independence because peculiar qualifications are essential and permanent tenure reduces dependence on appointing authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: select modes of choice for judges that best secure necessary qualifications; accept some inter-branch appointment connections if they improve judicial competence and independence through tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound republic / federal division yields 'double security'
rubrics_metrics.description: In the compound republic of America the power surrendered by the People is first divided between two distinct Governments (federal and state), and then the portion allotted to each subdivided among distinct departments; hence a double security arises to the rights of the People.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: federalism — dividing authority vertically between national and state governments — creates mutual controls between governments in addition to internal departmental checks, increasing protection of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarding minority rights by multiplicity of interests and classes (pluralism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different interests necessarily exist in different classes; by comprehending many separate descriptions of citizens, an unjust combination of a majority of the whole is rendered improbable; multiplicity of interests protects civil rights in the same way multiplicity of sects protects religious rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two methods of guarding minority rights described: (1) create an authority independent of the society (less desirable), or (2) enlarge and diversify the society so many interests make unjust majorities unlikely (preferred). Size, variety of interests, and pluralism are recommended design tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larger extent of republic increases capacity for self-government (within practical limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The larger the society, provided it lie within a practical sphere, the more duly capable it will be of self-government; extent of country and number of People increase number of interests and sects and thus security for rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: a suitably extended republic, combined with federal principles, can enlarge the practicable sphere for self-government and reduce the danger of oppressive majorities in small jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice is the end of government; institutional design must protect civil and religious rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is the end of Government and civil society; security for civil rights must be the same as that for religious rights — i.e., multiplicity of interests and sects provide protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative endpoint: institutional arrangements (separation of powers, federalism, pluralism) should be justified by and oriented toward securing justice and protecting rights across society.
